title: Verifying an Alien Dictionary
description:
In an alien language, words use the same 26 lowercase English letters, but possibly in a different lexicographical `order` (a permutation of `'a'` through `'z'`).

Given an array of strings `words` and the alien alphabet `order`, return `true` if and only if `words` is sorted in non-decreasing lexicographical order according to `order`.

A word `a` comes before word `b` if at the first index where they differ, `a[i]` appears earlier than `b[i]` in `order`. If one word is a prefix of the other, the shorter word must come first; equal words are considered sorted.
constraints: All characters in words[i] and order are lowercase English letters ('a'-'z').
order is a permutation of all 26 lowercase English letters.
hints: Precompute a 26-element rank array mapping each letter 'a'..'z' to its index in order.
Because lexicographical order is transitive, checking that every adjacent pair (words[i], words[i + 1]) is in valid order is sufficient.
Don't forget the prefix edge case: if two adjacent words match across the entire length of the shorter word, the first word must not be longer than the second.

examples.explanation: At index 0, 'h' appears before 'l' in the alien alphabet, so ["hello", "leetcode"] is sorted.
Between "word" and "world", the first differing characters are 'd' and 'l'; since 'd' comes after 'l' in order, return false.
"app" is a prefix of "apple", so "apple" cannot precede "app"; return false.
